provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Termination of Parental Rights to PML and EGL
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed termination, holding that whether the Department made reasonable efforts is assessed case by case, that its efforts must be accessible and tailored to the parent, and that a case plan adapted to a mother's intellectual disability satisfied the standard.
key_cases.relevance: Reasonable, unsuccessful efforts are an element the State must prove by clear and convincing evidence under § 14-2-309(a)(iii).
key_cases.quote: We assess on a case-by-case basis whether sufficient evidence exists to demonstrate the Department made reasonable efforts to rehabilitate the family

key_cases.case_name: LS v. Johnson County Department of Family Services
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed a jury verdict terminating parental rights, holding that termination statutes are strictly scrutinized and must be proved by clear and convincing evidence, and that neglect is assessed cumulatively rather than incident by incident.
key_cases.relevance: States the clear-and-convincing burden and the cumulative-evidence rule governing termination on abuse or neglect grounds.
key_cases.quote: Considering the evidence in the record in its entirety, there is clear and convincing proof sufficient to support the jury's findings of abuse and neglect

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed an adoption granted without the mother's consent, holding the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding clear and convincing evidence that she willfully failed to support her child under Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 1-22-110(a).
key_cases.relevance: Supplies the Wyoming standard for adoption without parental consent, the alternative route to severing parental rights outside Title 14.
key_cases.quote: The district court did not abuse its discretion by concluding there was clear and convincing evidence that Mother willfully failed to support her child

key_cases.case_name: In the Matter of the Adoption of ATWS
key_cases.holding: The Court reversed the denial of an adoption petition, holding the adoption statutes, read in light of their purpose of providing for the welfare of children, do not bar the petitioner from adopting where the existing parent's rights would be unaffected, and remanded for a best-interests determination.
key_cases.relevance: Removes a legal barrier to adoption where the child's existing legal parent retains rights, expanding permanency options.
key_cases.quote: The adoption statutes, whose purpose of providing for the welfare of children is the surest guide to their meaning, do not prohibit KA from adopting the Child

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that before a State may permanently sever the rights of parents in their natural child, the Due Process Clause requires proof of the State's allegations by at least clear and convincing evidence.
key_cases.relevance: This is the federal constitutional floor that Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 14-2-309's clear-and-convincing standard implements at the termination decision.
key_cases.quote: due process requires that the State support its allegations by at least clear and convincing evidence

state_agency.name: Wyoming Department of Family Services
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the DFS field office in the county where the child lives — the list is at dfs.wyo.gov/about/contact-us

extended_foster_care_age: Ends at 18; to 19 only if graduating (Wyo. DFS IV-E policy); court may order care or transitional services to 21 (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-431(b))

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
